## TL;DR

Added a persistent rule that UI verification by engineers must not open a desktop browser or use the human's Chrome profile. The rule is in the repository guidance and built-in engineer prompt, with a regression test. Also removed `repoos init`'s automatic system-browser launch; init now prints the ready URL. The changed-path check built successfully and its first test pass completed with 561 files and 8,030 tests passing (one skipped). The runner began the check wrapper's second pass, but its shell session closed before returning the final status. RepoOS should reverify during handoff.

## Work and rationale

The durable policy is in `AGENTS.md` as a concise rule with a link to `docs/agent-ui-and-preview-conventions.md`. The longer guidance explicitly prohibits `open` and `xdg-open` on URLs, headed browser launches, and use of the user's Chrome profile. It directs interactive verification to headless Playwright using its bundled browser, including QA and preview work on auth-less local servers. `AGENTS.md` remains below its 30 KB limit (27,510 bytes after the edit).

The built-in engineer instructions live in `src/core/config.ts` in `DEFAULT_AGENTS`; I added the same restriction there. `src/ui-app/tests/default-agent-prompts.test.ts` now asserts the prohibition and the required Playwright alternative, so a future prompt change cannot silently drop the rule.

A source search found `src/commands/init.ts`'s `openBrowser` helper, called when the init wizard's console server became ready. That helper ran `open`, `cmd /c start`, or `xdg-open` with the URL. Since init may be run by an engineer and has no reason to take over the desktop, I removed the launcher and now print the console URL from `onReady`. The support route's remaining `xdg-open` use opens a selected directory in a support workflow; it does not open URLs and is not the QA/preview behavior addressed here. Playwright scripts found in the repository use headless launch options.

`repoos.toml` was left untouched, as required. The active task transcript was not available in this worktree: `.repoos` contained only `canary.txt`, and no tracked transcript files were present. Therefore I could not substantiate which exact command or browser channel caused the reported incident. The repository-owned init launcher was nevertheless a concrete focus-stealing path and is now removed.

## Approaches tried

I searched source, scripts, `justfile`, docs, and the worktree's available `.repoos` data for `open`/`xdg-open`, headed Playwright settings, Chrome channel selection, the reported preview URL, and recent transcript markers. This distinguished URL launch behavior from unrelated UI `window.open` calls, intentional support-folder opening, and headless Playwright test harnesses. I considered leaving init's behavior intact because it is an interactive wizard, but it can be invoked unattended and its automatic launch conflicts with the task's no-focus-stealing requirement. Printing the URL preserves discoverability without controlling the user's desktop.

## Challenges and blockers

The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` ran on the remote validation runner. The build completed, then the first test pass reported 561 passed files and 8,030 passed tests, with one skipped. The wrapper then started another test pass. The local command session subsequently disappeared, so I could not observe the final check summary or exit status. No failing test output was observed before that point. The handoff server-side check must confirm the final result.

The requested transcript investigation was limited by the absence of transcript artifacts in this worktree; no claim is made about the original agent's exact browser command. No preview or headed browser was launched during this work.

## Key learnings

A repo can contain a desktop-launch path even when its serve script does not open anything: `repoos init` owned a deferred `onReady` URL opener. Removing the implicit launch is safer for interactive and unattended runs alike, while printing the URL keeps the next action clear. The default agent prompt and the repository-wide guidance serve different entry points, so both need the same explicit language and a test should pin the prompt contract. Searches also need to distinguish URL openers from other platform actions such as opening a support directory.
